title: Shorter sliding windows (S = seq//4) on the r1 config
description: One line in _compute_window_sizes (short_window = long_window // 4, i.e. 1024 -> 512) on top of the round-1 replicated config (HEAD_DIM 64, TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128).
reflection: val_bpb 0.989668 at queued_s 1643 - the deepest queue slot of the round, so this is a conservative measurement. 486.5M tokens, 1856 steps, MFU 35.89%, peak VRAM 45.0GB. Control is round 1's four byte-identical runs (mean 0.993849, sd 0.000584, mean 469.5M tokens): delta -0.004181, i.e. 7.2 sd, and the best number in the cell (beats the 0.992664 cold-card baseline by -0.003). The effect DECOMPOSES, and the second half is the interesting part. Tokens: the within-cluster slope (-0.000128 bpb/1M) predicts 0.991673 at 486.5M. I measured 0.989668, so -0.0020 is genuine quality beyond throughput. That is the first positive quality residual anyone has measured in this cell - HEAD_DIM 64 and the 2^18 batch both came in AT or BELOW their token prediction. Read: prepare.py best-fit-packs several documents per 2048-token row and fa3.flash_attn_func is given causal+window only, with NO document block mask, so attention span beyond a token's own document lands on unrelated text. Shrinking 6 of 8 layers from 1024 to 512 removes mostly-noise context while the two full-2048 layers (3 and 7, including the last) keep global mixing. Caveat I want on the record: I predicted ~505M tokens and got 486.5M. FLOPs/token fell 7.9% (239.3M -> 220.4M) but tokens rose only 3.6% over the cluster mean, because MFU dropped 37.6% -> 35.9% - the shorter window makes the FA3 kernel less efficient, so roughly half the FLOP saving was eaten. That matters for the follow-up: going to seq//8 would buy almost no further throughput, so the only reason to try it is the quality residual, and that is a different and less certain bet. The cheaper follow-ups are the orthogonal ones - a0's and a1's MATRIX_LR bracket composes with this, and WINDOW_PATTERN itself (more S layers, e.g. SSSSSSSL) is untouched.
